title: The Rock Cycle
seo_title: Grade 7 Rock Cycle Worksheets: Igneous, Sedimentary and Metamorphic Rocks
standard_text: Develop a model to describe the cycling of Earth's materials and the flow of energy that drives this process.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on the rock cycle (NGSS MS-ESS2-1): igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks, the processes that change them, and the energy from Earth's interior and the sun. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Rocks change from one type to another.
key_sub: Melting and cooling, weathering and deposition, and heat and pressure cycle Earth's materials, driven by Earth's heat and the sun.
body_html:
How to think about it

Rocks are constantly changing in the rock cycle:

  • Igneous rock forms when melted rock (magma or lava) cools and hardens (examples: granite, basalt, obsidian).
  • Sedimentary rock forms when sediments are deposited in layers, then compacted and cemented (examples: sandstone, limestone, shale).
  • Metamorphic rock forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting (examples: marble, slate, gneiss).

Energy drives the cycle: heat from Earth's interior melts rock and causes metamorphism; energy from the sun (with gravity) drives weathering, erosion and deposition.

Example

Lava cools into black glassy rock. What type?

Cooling melted rock.

Answer: igneous

Example

Shale is heated and squeezed into slate. Which process?

Heat and pressure, no melting.

Answer: metamorphism

Common mistakes

  • Thinking rocks never change.
  • Thinking metamorphic rock forms by melting.
  • Thinking the sun melts rocks into magma. Earth's interior heat does.

faq.q: What are the three types of rock?
faq.a: Igneous (cooled magma or lava), sedimentary (compacted and cemented sediments) and metamorphic (changed by heat and pressure).

faq.q: What energy drives the rock cycle?
faq.a: Heat from Earth's interior drives melting and metamorphism; energy from the sun drives weathering and erosion.

faq.q: Can a sedimentary rock become igneous?
faq.a: Yes. If it is buried deep enough to melt, the magma can cool to form igneous rock.
